corpus.rawAudioAndTranscripts: Ignored local data only; omitted from this evidence.

method.latency: Median warm latency per clip across three measured rounds. Timing starts inside the browser callback after Playwright transfers the audio bytes, and includes decode, preprocessing and inference.
method.quality: Word error rate (WER), lower is better.
method.acceptanceRule: Ship only a variant with improved quality and no increase in warm latency; the aspirational usable-latency target is at least 20% lower than baseline.

decision: Retain the production whisper-base q8 configuration. Trim and DSP slightly improve overall WER but increase latency; q4 improves WER with substantially higher latency; tinyguard is faster with materially worse WER; chunking is worse on both measures. No candidate meets the acceptance rule.
limitations: Results describe this 56-clip local corpus and the measured machine/runtime only.
The corpus condition was clean; performance under noisy speech conditions is not established.
No per-clip values, audio, reference transcripts or hypotheses are included in public evidence.
Subsequent owner device acceptance and the untested Apple/iPhone reminder are tracked separately in speech-device-evidence.json.
